value: Measure fio IOPS, bandwidth, and tail latency across a yaml sweep
Validates that each fio JSON job completes and parses IOPS, bandwidth, and clat percentiles. This is storage I/O, not a memory test
#1: IOPS mean (iops_mean); #2: Bandwidth, MB/s, by block size (bandwidth_mb_s); #3: Completion latency p50, us (clat_p50_us)
Run the system fio executable with --output-format=json and libaio against yaml filename

Run apt-installed fio --output-format=json --ioengine=libaio against yaml filename (default data/fio_target.bin), expanding the cartesian yaml rw x block_size x io_depth sweep with size, num_jobs, and runtime, to measure IOPS, bandwidth, and completion-latency percentiles. This is file-backed storage I/O, not a DRAM microbenchmark

Run fio --output-format=json --ioengine=libaio against yaml filename, expanding the cartesian rw, block_size, and io_depth sweep with size, num_jobs, and runtime, to measure IOPS, bandwidth, and clat percentiles. This is file-backed storage I/O, not a DRAM test. warmup_duration_sec and stonewall are not passed to fio

Cartesian fio sweep writing JSON jobs against a file target (default data/fio_target.bin), not necessarily a raw /dev/nvme device. io_engine: libaio. filename: target path. direct: 1. rw/block_size/io_depth: swept from yaml lists. size: job file size (smoke 64m, baseline 1g). runtime: seconds (smoke 5, baseline 15). num_jobs: parallel jobs. warmup_duration_sec, stonewall, and sync_mode are yaml fields and are not passed to fio. time_based is enabled
fio JSON stdout plus a normalized CSV row per sweep point
one CSV row per rw, block_size, and io_depth job

field_name: run_benchmark Command Plus Options for Smoke Run
value: bash run_benchmark.sh --smoke --validate --io-engine libaio --filename data/fio_target.bin --direct 1 --sync-mode async --rw randread --block-size 4k --size 64m --io-depth 1,8 --num-jobs 4 --warmup-duration-sec 0 --runtime 5 --time-based 1 --stonewall 1

field_name: run_benchmark Command Plus Options for Baseline Run
value: bash run_benchmark.sh --baseline --validate --io-engine libaio --filename data/fio_target.bin --direct 1 --sync-mode async --rw randread,randwrite --block-size 4k,8k --size 1g --io-depth 1,8,32 --num-jobs 4 --warmup-duration-sec 2 --runtime 15 --time-based 1 --stonewall 1

field_name: run_benchmark Command Plus Options for Extended Run
value: bash run_benchmark.sh --extended --validate --io-engine libaio --filename data/fio_target.bin --direct 1 --sync-mode async --rw randread,randwrite,read,write --block-size 4k,8k,128k --size 4g --io-depth 1,8,32,64 --num-jobs 4 --warmup-duration-sec 1 --runtime 12 --time-based 1 --stonewall 1
iops_mean, iops_p95, iops_p99, bandwidth_mb_s, clat_p50_us, clat_p99_us, clat_p999_us, p999_latency_ms
Every fio job exits with status=ok, nonzero IOPS, and a bandwidth_bytes value

iops_p95 and iops_p99 are left blank. clat percentiles come from fio's clat_ns percentile map, and p999_latency_ms is clat_p999_us divided by 1000. The headline metric columns on every row are the first rw/block/depth job; case_* keeps that row's own measurement. Default filename is data/fio_target.bin
NVIDIA H100 SXM host (20+ vCPUs, 128+ GB RAM, local NVMe), 1x H100 SXM (80 GB HBM3, sm_90, 132 SMs)
Bash, SQLite, Python, PyYAML, Flexible I/O Tester (FIO), libaio
Default target is a regular file under data/. Raw NVMe is optional. Warmup/stonewall/sync_mode yaml fields are not passed to fio
